routes.description: Present objective moral facts and duties, moral knowledge, moral transformation, and moral rationality as a connected body of evidence, then compare classical theism with secular ethical accounts under abductive explanatory criteria.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the four moral phenomena warrant explanation, classical theism is a legitimate explanatory candidate, and its account of their authority, accessibility, transformative horizon, and relation to fulfillment provides qualified comparative support for theism.

motionBridge.description: Comparative explanation of the four moral phenomena must provide at least a qualified increase in the plausibility of classical theism within a cumulative case.

centralBridges.description: Objective value and categorical obligation, moral knowledge, moral transformation, and morality’s rational relation to fulfillment must be established as genuine explananda.
A morally perfect, omniscient, and omnipotent creator must qualify as a coherent candidate capable of explaining the identified moral phenomena.
The theistic account must explain the authority and breadth of moral experience better than naturalistic, cultural, instrumental, or axiomatic alternatives.
The comparative advantage must remain evidentially relevant after accounting for prior plausibility, an incomplete candidate pool, combined alternatives, and the argument’s cumulative role.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Moral phenomenology and properly basic moral apprehension must support irreducible categorical authority rather than merely chosen goals or social conditioning.
Theism must offer resources for complete moral transformation and for harmony between moral life and ultimate human fulfillment.

routes.description: Challenge both the proposed moral explananda and the admission of God into the explanatory comparison while showing how well-being, empathy, culture, natural processes, and disciplined inquiry can account for moral judgment and change.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if theism lacks demonstrated candidacy or comparative explanatory advantage, or if secular accounts adequately accommodate the four moral phenomena while theistic grounding leaves additional epistemic, methodological, or hiddenness problems.

motionBridge.description: The four moral phenomena must fail to provide a warranted comparative inference from moral experience to classical theism.

centralBridges.description: God’s eligibility and the adequacy of the explanatory candidate pool must be justified before comparative abduction can support a theistic conclusion.
Well-being, empathy, shared physical needs, learning, culture, and natural processes must adequately explain moral evaluation, conscience, knowledge, and ordinary transformation.
Objective means-end assessment after adopting foundational values must remain viable without an additional divine source of categorical obligation.
Problems of divine identification, access to divine requirements, unconstrained supernatural hypotheses, and hiddenness must defeat the claimed theistic advantage.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Variation in guilt and moral intuition must support cultural and psychological explanations rather than an inference to universally apprehended divine authority.
Any comparative conclusion must be constrained by priors, bad-lot concerns, combined secular alternatives, and the limited reach of moral intuition.

sections.title: Abductive Method, Candidate Pool, and Conclusion
sections.rationale: This issue governs whether classical theism may enter the explanatory comparison, how candidate-pool and prior-plausibility constraints apply, and what qualified conclusion comparative success could support.

sections.title: Objective Moral Facts and Categorical Authority
sections.rationale: The principal ontological clash concerns whether binding moral obligations are irreducibly categorical and call for a personal moral ground, or can be understood through foundational values and objective relations to well-being.

sections.title: Moral Knowledge, Guilt, and Conscience
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether moral axioms, guilt, and apparent authority disclose genuine moral truths requiring theistic explanation or arise adequately through empathy, culture, learning, and shared human conditions.

sections.title: Moral Transformation and Its Horizon
sections.rationale: Transformation is an express part of the motion, requiring comparison between theistic hope for complete moral formation and secular mechanisms that produce behavioral and character change.

sections.title: Moral Rationality, Flourishing, and Scope
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether morality is rationally congruent with ultimate fulfillment and whether flourishing-based accounts can cover categorical duties, animal suffering, character, and apparent conflicts between morality and self-interest.

sections.title: Comparative Worldview Fit and Theistic Liabilities
sections.rationale: The final comparison integrates explanatory breadth with challenges involving divine identification, access, methodological restraint, hiddenness, naturalistic reduction, and the cumulative evidential role claimed for morality.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Theism and secular ethical theories should be compared by standard explanatory criteria for their accounts of moral facts, knowledge, transformation, and rationality.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Comparative explanatory superiority cannot overcome a sufficiently low intrinsic probability, so the moral evidence supplies at most a qualified reason for theism within the total evidence.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: The relevant transformation question is not whether ordinary moral improvement occurs, but whether secular naturalism can sustain realistic hope for complete moral transformation.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Objective moral values are intrinsically good, whereas objective moral duties are binding and authoritative prescriptions that can impose categorical requirements without exception.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: The phenomenology of guilt can provide evidence of genuine wrongdoing and moral authority rather than being exhausted by an account in terms of cultural conditioning.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: Exceptionally obvious foundational moral principles can be rationally accepted as properly basic axioms from which further ethical reasoning proceeds without inferential proof.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: Some moral obligations are categorical requirements and therefore cannot be reduced to instrumental reasoning about how to achieve goals that an agent has already chosen.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: An account restricted to human flourishing is morally too narrow because animal suffering and the formation of a person's moral character can also matter intrinsically.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Binding, objective, prescriptive moral obligations call for explanation, and a loving creator who enables moral apprehension offers an account of their authority.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Theistic ethics requires a morally perfect, maximally great God rather than an arbitrary deity, and moral considerations can help distinguish that hypothesis from finite or capricious gods.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-09.proposition: Divine hiddenness may reflect relational priorities beyond producing bare belief in God's existence, because recognizing that someone exists is not equivalent to having a relationship.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: The abductive case has not justified either that the asserted moral phenomena require further explanation or that God qualifies as a reasonable candidate explanation.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Moral transformation can occur through secular natural processes, and even a false belief in divine supervision could motivate behavioral improvement.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Culturally variable guilt cannot ground objective morality, while actions can still be assessed objectively by their effects on adopted goals such as survival and well-being.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Empathy, universalization, and role reversal can explain conscience and much apparent moral authority without religious commands or a further supernatural foundation.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: Human-benefiting axioms can generate coherent ethical systems and could arise under godless physical conditions because creatures with shared needs have reasons to converge on them.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: Once concern for well-being is adopted, actions can be evaluated by whether they advance or frustrate that goal without introducing additional categorical oughts.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Methodological naturalism permits demonstrated supernatural causes but rejects an unexplained deity that adds mystery without predictive or explanatory power.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Positing God as morality's foundation does not resolve moral disagreement unless people can reliably identify the good deity and access that deity's requirements.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-01.proposition: Confidence in an abductive conclusion should be proportioned to the quality and depth of the available pool of candidate explanations.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-06.proposition: Persistent divine hiddenness is morally unexpected if a good creator could clarify a consequential dispute whose prolonged uncertainty causes harm.
